blocking.section: Observability (Elastic Logstash row); Request and response transformation (Gzip compression row); Authentication and authorization (JWT token signing row); Summary
blocking.issue: Acceptance criterion 7 fails. Several Ruralz mechanism cells name no kind, Policy type or Filter defined in the Configuration model. The Elastic Logstash cell names no kind or type. The Gzip compression and JWT token signing cells name only a hypothetical "built-in ... Policy type" that the registry does not contain. They also do not name the kind that would carry it, which the document's own Method rule 4 requires. The Summary therefore overclaims when it says every row names its carrier. An architect following these three rows into docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md finds nothing to trace.
blocking.evidence: Line 310: "| Elastic Logstash | Yes | Yes | Planned (M1) | JSON access log records on stdout, or OTLP logs |". Line 148: "| Gzip compression | No | Yes | Planned (M5) | A built-in compression Filter registered as a new Policy type |". Line 209: "| JWT token signing | Yes | Yes | Planned (M2) | A built-in signing Policy type; keys never sit in `plugin` `config` |". Line 30 (Summary): "Each row names the kind, Policy type or Filter that carries it." Line 62 (rule 4): "Where a row needs a field that does not exist yet, the mechanism names the kind that would carry it".
blocking.fix: Elastic Logstash: "Access log records selected by `Gateway` `telemetry.accessLog`, written as JSON on stdout, or OTLP logs from `Gateway` `telemetry.otlp`". Gzip compression: "A `Policy` of a new built-in compression type (OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-3), attached at `Gateway` or `Route` scope and run in `onResponse`". JWT token signing: "A `Policy` of a new built-in signing type attached to the `Route` (OQ-security-and-identity-11), with keys held as `secretRef` and never in `plugin` `config`". Keep the Summary sentence only once every row meets it.

blocking.section: Request and response transformation (Mocked data, Workflows); Routing (Configurable client redirects); AI gateway (LLM routing, multi-routing, and aggregation); Services connectivity (SOAP integration); Traffic management (Concurrent calls); Gaps and non-goals (Partial parity)
blocking.issue: The document labels only eight rows "Partial parity", and evaluators rely on that label because the status column alone reads as full parity. At least six more planned rows deliver less than the KrakenD feature, and their own Notes cells or dependency documents say so, but they carry no label and are missing from the Partial parity paragraph. Workflows covers linear workflows only, and dependency graphs are OQ-data-plane-3. Concurrent calls becomes delayed hedging, limited to idempotent requests with replayable bodies (Traffic management and resilience, Hedging). Mocked data, a built-in CE feature, needs a user-written WASM Plugin. Route-issued client redirects need a `plugin` Policy. The CEL `body` variable is JSON-only (Configuration model, Variables), so the SOAP mechanism cannot read an XML envelope. LLM aggregation is buffered only, under the proposed option of OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-7. An evaluator who counts Partial parity rows to size migration risk gets the wrong number.
blocking.evidence: Line 376: "Eight planned rows are narrower than the KrakenD feature; each Notes/ADR cell says how." Line 165: "`composition.mode: sequential` with per-step `when` for linear workflows | Dependency graphs per OQ-data-plane-3". Line 278: "Request hedging on the `Upstream` leg for idempotent, replayable requests". Line 164: "A `plugin` Policy that short-circuits a request Phase with a static response". Line 200: "Route-issued redirects use a `plugin` Policy". Line 258: "`transform.request` and `transform.response` build and read XML envelopes", while the Configuration model defines `request.body` as "(JSON as `dyn`, body Phases and composition only)". Line 461: "(a) Buffered aggregation only, no streaming (proposed)".
blocking.fix: Start each of these six Notes/ADR cells with "Partial parity:" followed by what is missing. Workflows: "linear workflows only; dependency graphs per OQ-data-plane-3". Concurrent calls: "a delayed hedge, not N simultaneous calls; idempotent, replayable requests only". Mocked data: "static responses need a user-written `plugin` Policy until OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-3". Configurable client redirects: "Route-issued redirects need a `plugin` Policy". SOAP integration: "CEL can build an XML request, but reading an XML response needs an XML decoder the Configuration model lacks"; add XML body decoding as an explicit sub-question of OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-1. LLM routing: "aggregation buffered only, pending OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-7". Then change "Eight planned rows" to the new count (fourteen) and add one sentence per new row to the Partial parity paragraph.

blocking.section: Services connectivity (section intro and Lambda, Azure Service Bus, Amazon SNS rows); Gaps and non-goals (Not planned rows)
blocking.issue: The matrix misrepresents the scope and status of the dependency Open question it relies on for most of its Not planned rows. In Multi-protocol, OQ-multi-protocol-14 asks only about AMQP, Google Cloud Pub/Sub and Amazon SQS. It is still open, with option (a) marked current, and it is marked "Blocking: Yes, for the parity matrix". The matrix says that question's option (a) keeps all seven rows out of M0 to M5, and presents that as settled. The seven include Lambda, which the matrix itself assigns to OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-10, and Azure Service Bus and Amazon SNS, which OQ-multi-protocol-14 does not name. The "Decisions these counts record" list never records that this matrix adopts option (a). An evaluator therefore cannot tell whether these six Not planned rows are decided or still pending.
blocking.evidence: Line 241: "the seven Not planned rows are cloud queues and functions with no researched Go library, which OQ-multi-protocol-14 option (a) keeps out of M0 to M5." Line 370: "No researched Go library; OQ-multi-protocol-14 option (a) keeps them out of M0 to M5". docs/architecture/07-multi-protocol.md line 585: "| OQ-multi-protocol-14 | Should AMQP, Google Cloud Pub/Sub or Amazon SQS join `Upstream.spec.protocol`? | (a) Not planned in M0 to M5 (current); (b) New values by ADR; (c) Plugins | multi-protocol | Yes, for the parity matrix |".
blocking.fix: Rewrite the intro sentence as: "the seven Not planned rows have no researched Go library: six brokers and cloud queues under OQ-multi-protocol-14, whose current option (a) this matrix adopts, and Lambda under OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-10." Add a bullet to "Decisions these counts record": "OQ-multi-protocol-14: option (a) adopted for AMQP consumer and producer, Google Cloud Pub/Sub and Amazon SQS. Azure Service Bus and Amazon SNS follow the same reasoning; Multi-protocol should extend the question to name them." Make the same wording change in the Gaps and non-goals row.

blocking.issue: The rule contradicts foundation pack section 1 and the matrix's own FIPS row. The pack defines the FIPS build as a separate build flavor published as separate artifacts, and says "no enterprise build" means no feature difference, not a single binary. "The single public build" tells evaluators there is only one build, which contradicts the Security section's `GOFIPS140` build flavor row.
blocking.evidence: Line 64: "Every Planned row is free under Apache-2.0 in the single public build ([ADR-0002](...), P1)." Foundation pack section 1: "FIPS build | A build flavor (`GOFIPS140`, Planned (M5)) with the same features and license as the default build, published as separate artifacts; \"no enterprise build\" means no feature difference, not a single binary". Line 173: "`GOFIPS140` build flavor of `ruralzd`".
blocking.fix: Replace the phrase with: "Every Planned row is free under Apache-2.0 with the same feature set in every public build, including the FIPS build ([ADR-0002](../adr/0002-apache-2-license-no-feature-gating.md), P1)."

non_blocking.suggestion: "Session memory of 96 KiB or less (target)" agrees with the Roadmap M3 scope and with Performance budgets and benchmarking (Memory budget). It does not agree with Multi-protocol line 293, which says "about 96 KiB (hypothesis)". Cite the owner so the figure is traceable: "Session memory of 96 KiB or less (target) ([Performance budgets](../architecture/12-performance-budgets-and-benchmarking.md#memory-budget))". Also flag the upstream tagging conflict to Multi-protocol rather than changing the tag here.

"Macros such as `geoIP()` map to CEL variables and `authz.geoip`" reads as if a geography CEL variable exists. The Configuration model's variables (`request`, `source`, `route`, `consumer`, `auth`, ...) carry no country. Say that `geoIP()` maps only to a separate `authz.geoip` allow or deny, and that a rule combining geography with other conditions needs a `plugin` Policy.

The KrakenD cell "Async agents for AMQP and, in EE, Kafka" makes a vendor claim with no URL on its line. Append ([source](https://www.krakend.io/docs/async/amqp/)) and ([source](https://www.krakend.io/features/)), both present in the research files.

For evaluators, add one column or sentence counting the Planned rows that wait on a blocking Open question. OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-1 covers seven M1 EE-only transformation rows. OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-3, -6, -8 and -9 cover M5 rows. The M1 share of 34% (target) partly depends on OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-1, whose option (b) would turn several rows Not planned.

Data plane precedence rank 5 counts `when` as a constraint, so a `when`-only Route ties with any Route that has no host or path and one constraint, and rank 6 (`metadata.name`) then decides. The catch-all is not guaranteed to rank lowest. State this, or tell authors to name the catch-all so it sorts last.
